body:
The user's story has the price range roughly right and the cause and timing wrong. **UBL is United Breweries Ltd, the Kingfisher beer maker. It does not compete with Radico in spirits.** The story probably confuses UBL with the UB Group / United Spirits (USL) / Vijay Mallya saga. That ran mainly from 2012 to 2016. Diageo agreed in November 2012 to buy 53.4% of USL, but its open offer failed and it ended up with about 25% by July 2013 ([Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/companies/diageo-seals-deal-with-mallya-to-pick-up-53-4-112110900175_1.html); [Business Standard Jul 2013](https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/diageo-gains-control-over-united-spirits-ups-stake-to-25-113070400973_1.html)). The real "UB connection" is older. In the 1990s, Lalit Khaitan approached United Spirits for a partnership after Radico's Shaw Wallace bottling contract expired and was refused, which pushed Radico to build its own brands. **8PM whisky launched in August 1998** ([StockEdge](https://blog.stockedge.com/stock-insights-radico-khaitan-ltd/)). The research found **no source showing investors bought Radico in 2008 on a UB thesis**. That version is most likely investor folklore.

The price record shows something more useful than the legend. Adjusted prices fell **from a 2008 high of ₹191 to a low of ₹49.6 (−74%)**. They then spent **2010–2016 trading between about ₹76 and ₹186**. Closing prices were then ₹294 (2017), ₹400 (2018), ₹1,236 (2021), ₹2,606 (2024) and ₹3,298 (2025) ([stockpricearchive](https://stockpricearchive.com/share-price-history-and-returns/radico/)). Recent quotes are around ₹4,135–4,196, against a 52-week high near ₹4,748 ([screener.in](https://www.screener.in/company/RADICO/)). Aggregator data is inconsistent, so check the exact multiples on NSE/BSE. "120 → 4,600" is achievable on an entry anywhere in 2010–2016. A 2008 buyer, though, first lost three-quarters of their money and then waited eight years.

`insight:value-trap-patterns` | 2026-11-19 | tickers: - | confidence: verified

Patterns from Yes Bank, Credit Suisse, GE, Jet Airways, Future Retail, PC Jeweller, Zee, Reliance Capital, Paytm, Evergrande: (1) Low P/B in a lender with understated NPAs -- book value is fictional (Yes Bank divergence; CS at 0.2x TBV); (2) Low P/E on low-quality earnings -- receivable factoring, contract assets, non-GAAP adjustments (GE, Valeant); (3) Dividend yield funded by debt -- dividend > FCF (GE 2017, Evergrande); (4) 'Asset value' that needs a buyer: land banks, brands, airline slots, spectrum (Unitech, Kingfisher brand collateral, RCom spectrum) -- in distress, asset values fall with the company; (5) Promoter-levered good business -- great franchise, bad stock while pledges overhang (Zee); (6) Equity ahead of a restructuring -- debt converts, lenders or IBC wipe equity (Jet, Future, RCap, DHFL); (7) Structural decline mistaken for cyclical trough (print media, legacy telecom); (8) Post-IPO decline in insider-sold story stocks -- 'it's 70% off' is not cheap if it was 5x overpriced (Paytm). Tests: is FCF positive and covering dividends? Is debt falling? Is the 'asset' saleable today at book? Is the promoter unlevered? Piotroski F >= 7 and Z > 2.99 for value buys; else require a dated catalyst. Counter-example: genuine turnarounds (e.g., Suzlon after deleveraging) needed debt actually extinguished, not promised.

`person:michael-burry` | confidence: **verified** | tags: us, process, value, contrarian, blowup

Scion Capital (Nov 2000-2008): +489.34% net of fees to June 2008 vs ~2-3% for the S&P 500 incl. dividends; investors made ~$700m+, Burry ~$100m. Early gains came from deep value and shorting dot-com stocks (2001 +55% per a blog, less reliable). Signature trade: from May 2005 bought credit default swaps on subprime mortgage bonds (first $60m from Deutsche Bank) after reading the actual loan pools in prospectuses; investors revolted and he side-pocketed positions during 2006-07 losses before the payoff; he exited CDS by April 2008. Structural edge: a tiny, unconstrained fund able to buy obscure securities; process edge: reads primary documents others skip, EV/EBITDA-style deep value screens, willingness to look wrong for 2+ years. Later: GameStop stake 2019 (sold before most of the 2021 squeeze); public 'crash' warnings repeatedly early (e.g., 2023 'Sell' tweet and index puts); deregistered Scion Asset Management in Nov 2025 after bearish AI-hyperscaler depreciation calls. Mistakes: investor-relations failure in 2006-07; serial premature macro calls. Copyable: read the annual report, notes and loan/collateral disclosures yourself; size contrarian bets so you can survive being early. Do not copy: public doom predictions as a timing tool.

body:
- **Catchment:** 52% of stores are in Tier III towns (<200k population) `[PPT-Q2]`. A Tier III town of 100–200k supports one ~17k sq ft store at ₹17 cr/year, which is about ₹850–1,700 per head per year of catchment. Plausible only if the store draws from surrounding villages (40–50 km radius on market days). Ground check: ask shoppers where they came from.
- **Ticket and footfall** [EST]: ₹17.3 cr/store ÷ ₹875 average bill ≈ **~19,800 bills per store per month ≈ 650/day**, peaking on weekends and festivals. At about 30–40% conversion (typical value apparel/general retail; *unverified* benchmark), footfall is about 1,600–2,200 per day. That ties to security: 1–2 exit checkers per shift for 650 bills is consistent.
- **Competition:**
  - Kirana and unorganised traders are the main share donors. Management says the "largest bucket" of growth is new customers from "mom-and-pop stores" `[CC-Q3FY26]`.
  - Zudio (Trent) is the apparel overlap in Tier I/II. *Zudio store count and density were not checked this session* (open).
  - V2 Retail (founded by the original Vishal founder, see below) and V-Mart (VMART) compete head-on in Tier II/III North and East.
  - DMart overlaps in FMCG only in larger towns.
  - **Quick commerce:** VMM runs its own "quick commerce" from stores: 781 stores, 1.52 cr registered users, about 5% of revenue, a 2-hour SLA, roughly cash break-even `[PPT-Q2]`, `[HSIE]`. The mix is 70% grocery, so it dilutes gross margin. In metros quick commerce is 1.5–2% of store revenue; in Tier II/III, 3–4% `[ELARA]`.
- **Brand history matters for the consumer and the landlord.** The original Vishal Retail (founder Ram Chandra Agarwal) went into CDR in 2009 with about ₹730 cr debt. The business went to TPG/Shriram in 2010–11, then to Kedaara/Partners Group in 2018 (deal size unverified). Agarwal now runs V2 Retail. The same brand has failed once on debt-funded expansion. Today's version has no bank debt and leased stores, which is a different risk profile (Business Standard 2009 "Vishal promoter to exit in debt recast"; V2 Retail FY26 AR).
